title: provisional-safety-ledger-for-weight-kv-activation-cost-model
creator: Aditi Rao
description:
Problem: We observe repeated transient OOMs during bursty continuous-batching scenarios when tenant workloads shift from short-context to long-context chat workloads. Root cause appears to be the combined pressure of sizable KV cache growth plus temporary activation spikes while weights remain pinned in GPU memory. Existing soft-watermark heuristics trigger broad eviction only after latency SLOs are violated.

Proposal: Create a provisional safety ledger (lightweight accounting layer) that tracks per-tenant projected memory usage across three orthogonal buckets: weights-fixed, kv-dynamic, activations-transient. The ledger will consume a small reserved headroom budget that is replenished/consumed by predicted arrivals using a short-horizon predictor (exponential smoothing on recent sequence-length distribution and batch size).

Goals: 
- Maintain p99 latency SLOs by avoiding emergency evictions that stall K/V lookup paths.
- Reduce false-positive preemptions that hurt throughput for medium-confidence bursts.
- Provide transparent per-tenant telemetry for billing and capacity planning.

Implementation sketch: 
1) Cost model: represent weights as static cost (bytes on device), KV as a time-decaying allocation where each KV entry carries a TTL-weighted cost, activations as a per-request transient allocation proportional to sequence_length * activation_bytes_per_token.  Ledger aggregates these into an "effective-in-use" number.
2) Headroom policy: reserve a headroom pool per GPU node (configurable fraction) and per-tenant soft-credits. The node-level safety ledger enforces a conservative cap on sum(effective-in-use) <= node_capacity - emergency_margin. If cap would be exceeded, ledger tries three ordered mitigations: a) apply per-tenant soft backpressure (throttle new requests), b) compact KV entries with LRU window + compressed summaries, c) controlled activation shedding by favoring lower-batch paths.
3) Predictor: short-window EWMA for seq-length and batch-rate; fallback to percentile-based conservative forecast when input distribution is multimodal.
4) Observability: add token-level and request-level telemetry tags showing ledger decisions and credit balances. Export to Console for per-route dashboards and rollout traces.

Trade-offs and risks: 
- Conservative headroom lowers peak utilization and increases cost; we'll A/B test headroom fraction.
- Predictor failure modes could under/over provision; add rapid rollback and canary at 5% of nodes.
- Complexity: keep ledger API tiny (credit/add/release/query) to simplify integration with runtime.

Deliverables: design doc, runtime shim + unit tests, integration test that replays production traffic trace (1M requests) to validate OOM/latency reduction, rollout plan with canary and observability dashboards.
